policy: Emergency controls stop new risk while preserving permissionless exits. Every external state-mutating operation on a canonical V2 module is classified exactly once. RISK_INCREASING operations fail closed on every listed operation scope. RISK_REDUCING value exits (already-final, caller-owned value) are never scope-gated, never depend on registry or authority health, and freeze only on an affirmative protocol SHUTDOWN reading (EXIT_SHUTDOWN_ONLY, V2-SC-117 pull_settled_claim). NEUTRAL operations neither create exposure nor move value and are never scope-gated. Read paths are never gated. A pause only ever removes capabilities: the exits available while paused are a subset of those available while unpaused.

classes.RISK_INCREASING: Creates new exposure or mutates a not-yet-final outcome (claim creation, staking, verification, evidence, disputes, settlement, slashing, governance parameter changes). Fails closed on every scope in gates and conditionalGates.
classes.NEUTRAL: Authority wiring or a module-local toggle that neither creates exposure nor moves value. Never scope-gated.
classes.RISK_REDUCING: A permissionless exit of already-final, caller-owned value, or a protective action (pausing, nonce cancellation). Never scope-gated on the caller's own path.

gates.EXIT_SHUTDOWN_ONLY: Value exit: live under every scoped pause and protocol levels 1-2; frozen only while EmergencyController denies pull_settled_claim (level 3). Fails open on any dependency failure.

excluded.rationale: Pause authority itself (authority layer). Its pause/unpause surface is the source of every scoped gate and cannot be gated by itself; separation of powers is enforced by its own roles.
Pause authority itself (authority layer). Pause/unpause, scope tolerances, and the timelocked controller rewire are the emergency control plane and are covered by the V2-SC-067 drills.
Authority layer: registry-resolved modules read their pause authority from it. Gating it on that same authority would be circular; module replacement is already timelocked (REPLACEMENT_DELAY).
